current_news.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
current_news.facts: Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface. OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters. Aside from qualifying components for applications at depths of up to 3,000 meters, the project pinpointed interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies. The company states that the completion of the project builds on more than 15 years of experience in subsea electrification and more than 5 million operating hours with electrified subsea systems. The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface.

OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters.

Aside from qualifying components for applications at depths of up to 3,000 meters, the project pinpointed interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies.

The company states that the completion of the project builds on more than 15 years of experience in subsea electrification and more than 5 million operating hours with electrified subsea systems.

The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

source_index.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech

N0.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
N0.body:
Out with hydraulics, in with electric: OneSubsea, TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron have tested all-electric tech at depths up to 3,000 meters.
Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface.

OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters.

Aside from qualifying components for applications at depths of up to 3,000 meters, the project pinpointed interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies.

The company states that the completion of the project builds on more than 15 years of experience in subsea electrification and more than 5 million operating hours with electrified subsea systems.

The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .
